title: A price-discrimination order can define a small-business compensation trigger while local competition and retailer recovery remain open
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission Southern Glazer's Wine and Spirits settlement announcement, complaint, and proposed stipulated order
geography: Independent wine and spirits retailers and competing chain retailers in 26 U.S. states covered by the proposed order

observations.period: October 2, 2026 proposed stipulated order and settlement announcement

denominator.unit: Southern Glazer's FTC Robinson-Patman enforcement matter; public materials do not provide a complete count of affected independent retailers or paired transactions

market_scope.value: nearly all Southern wine and spirits sales to the five largest chain retailers in 26 states

alleged_mechanism.value: discounts and rebates available to large buyers were alleged to be inaccessible to small competitors; the complaint alleges higher prices for identical bottles sold to independent retailers and nearby large chains

compensation_trigger.value: paired transactions can trigger a violation when discrimination exceeds a state-specific operating-cost threshold or recurs above $5,000 in aggregate over 12 months

remedy_multiplier_and_duration.value: Southern can resolve a qualifying violation by paying 1.5 times the full aggregate price differential; if it does not redress and the FTC prevails, the proposed order provides for double the aggregate differential; independent monitoring lasts six years

conversion.unit: court approval, implementation, identified retailer claim, payment, price correction, inventory or customer effect, business survival, local competition, or household recovery

observations.method: Structured extraction from the FTC settlement announcement, complaint, and proposed stipulated order. Alleged pricing mechanism, order scope, compensation trigger, multiplier, monitoring period, and downstream firm/consumer outcomes are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The pricing practices are allegations and the stipulated order is proposed; it has force of law only when approved and signed by the district court. Public materials do not establish the affected-retailer denominator, price differentials, claims, payments, implementation, or competitive effects.
observations.subgroup: Small independent wine and spirits retailers buying from Southern while competing with large national or regional chains, including retailers near the paired chain transactions described by the FTC.
observations.counterinterpretation: Price differences can reflect lawful cost differences, service, volume, delivery, or other commercial terms; a compensation formula may deter conduct without restoring a retailer's lost sales, margin, customer base, or local competitive position.

related_sources.claim: The FTC case record identifies the Southern Glazer's Robinson-Patman matter and proposed stipulated order materials.
The redacted complaint contains the allegations concerning higher prices for identical products, large-chain discounts, and independent-retailer competition.

boundary: This record advances a bounded supplier-price-discrimination-to-compensation-control route for small independent retailers. It does not establish final court approval, retailer eligibility, payment, price correction, business survival, consumer prices, local competition, household benefit, or durable trust.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Canonical FTC settlement announcement URL string used as a stable source identifier; official case and complaint links are retained for reproduction.
